title: A Recipe for the Mixtape
premise: Ulyana Pemberton has one talent she trusts: baking feelings into bread, a gift inherited from the grandmother who raised her. When her grandmother dies, Ulyana finds a recipe card in the box that isn't for food — it's a set of instructions that, when followed, lets her hear the memories baked into the school's oldest walls, and what she hears is a cover-up: decades ago, the school board buried the death of a scholarship student and rewrote the record to protect a founding family. As Ulyana digs, she discovers her best friend Theo's family is on the receiving end of the board's hush money, forcing loyalty against truth. With graduation looming and the board moving to demolish the old wing — and the evidence inside it — Ulyana must bake one final loaf that forces the whole town to taste what really happened, at the cost of her grandmother's reputation and her own place in Millbrook.
about_author: Sebastian Crane is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent three years covering school board meetings no one attended. They write young adult fiction about kids who discover that adults keep secrets in the most ordinary places — filing cabinets, recipe boxes, minutes of meetings.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Opening day of senior spring at Pemberton Bakery: Ulyana bakes a 'grief loaf' for a funeral and a 'first-date sourdough' for a classmate, counting down 94 days to graduation. Grandma Ida's hands shake now, and the bakery's future is uncertain. Emotional beat: weary tenderness; Ulyana wants out of Millbrook but can't say it aloud.

chapters.title: The Card That Isn't Bread
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Cleaning the recipe box after Grandma Ida's stroke, Ulyana finds a card labeled 'For the East Wing Loaf' with instructions that read like directions for a person, not food: 'knead until the walls remember.' She follows it as a joke in the closed-off east wing of Millbrook High and hears voices in the flour dust. Beat: eerie wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Walls Remember
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The recipe works: baked in the east wing's ancient oven, the loaf lets Ulyana experience fragments of memory — a boy running through halls in 1979, a fall, adults whispering. She recognizes the school seal on an old letterhead in the vision. Beat: obsession ignites; grief for Grandma temporarily displaced by purpose.

chapters.title: Theo Knows Something
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Best friend Theo Vasquez notices Ulyana sneaking into school after hours and covers for her with a janitor — too smoothly. He warns her off the east wing without explaining why, and flinches when the Harrow family name comes up. Beat: first crack in their friendship; Theo's protective secrecy reads, to Ulyana, like guilt.

chapters.title: Ninety-Four Days, Minus One
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Hospital visit to Grandma Ida, who can only squeeze Ulyana's hand when shown the strange recipe card — but the squeeze means yes. A nurse mentions Ida once worked at the school cafeteria in the late seventies. Beat: Ulyana realizes her grandmother is inside this story, not just its author.

chapters.title: The Harrow Scholarship
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Library research: in 1979, scholarship student Elias Okafor died — officially 'an accident' — and the Harrow family endowed a memorial fund weeks later. The current board president is Margaret Harrow. Theo's mother manages the fund's books. Beat: the conspiracy gains shape and names; dread sets in.

chapters.title: Bread for Liars
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. School board meeting, where demolition of the east wing is fast-tracked for June — eleven days after graduation. Ulyana bakes a 'truth loaf' for the meeting and watches Margaret Harrow take a bite and go pale. Beat: Ulyana tastes power for the first time, and likes it more than she should.

chapters.title: Hush Money and Honey Cake
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts his mother, who admits the Vasquez family has taken monthly payments from the Harrow fund since his father's injury — silence bought with survival money. If Ulyana exposes the fund's origin, they lose everything. Beat: Theo chooses loyalty over truth, and hates himself for it.

chapters.title: The Recipe Has Three Parts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Deciphering the card fully: the memory loaf needs three bakings — the walls (done), a witness object, and 'the baker's own grief.' Part two requires something Elias owned. Beat: rising stakes; Ulyana understands the magic demands sacrifice, foreshadowing the ending's cost.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Archive
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Theo's alternating POV. Reluctant heist of the school basement archive to find Elias's confiscated jacket, still boxed in evidence from 1979. They nearly get caught by Margaret Harrow herself, who is shredding files at midnight. Beat: adrenaline and uneasy partnership; Theo sees what Ulyana saw and can't unsee it.

chapters.title: Elias
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Baking with the jacket, Ulyana lives Elias's last week: a brilliant kid who discovered the Harrows were falsifying scholarship records and skimming funds, who planned to report it, who fell — or was pushed — from the east wing stairwell. Beat: grief becomes righteous fury; Elias stops being a case file and becomes a boy.

chapters.title: Grandma's Confession
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Grandma Ida, lucid for one afternoon, confesses: she was the cafeteria worker who found Elias's body, was paid to stay quiet, and wrote the recipe as penance — a way to make the walls testify someday. 'I couldn't be brave then. Bake me brave now.' Beat: heartbreak; the mentor's sin reframes everything.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Margaret Harrow offers Theo a full ride to any college — generations of Harrow generosity — if he keeps Ulyana away from the June board vote. Theo almost says yes. His little sister's medication depends on the hush money. Beat: the theme made flesh; Theo's choice is genuinely impossible.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Theo reports the archive break-in anonymously; the school locks the east wing early and confiscates Ulyana's remaining recipe materials. Ulyana finds out it was him. Beat: lowest point between allies; betrayal that is also an act of love, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: Sourdough Starter, Dead
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Grandma Ida dies peacefully, and with her the bakery's hundred-year-old starter goes flat — every loaf Ulyana bakes comes out tasting of nothing. The magic, tied to Ida's line, seems dead. Beat: mourning; Ulyana loses grandmother, friend, evidence, and gift in one week.

chapters.title: The Third Ingredient
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Rereading the card, Ulyana understands the final ingredient: 'the baker's own grief, given freely' — she must bake her sorrow for Ida into the loaf, surrendering the comfort of it forever. Theo arrives at the bakery door with Elias's jacket, which he stole back from evidence. Beat: forgiveness offered but not yet accepted; hope rekindled.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ulyana and Theo rebuild trust while racing the demolition schedule: they need a public baking, witnesses, and the board vote. They recruit the janitor, the nurse, and two classmates whose families were also silenced. Beat: the heist-movie rally; belonging forged from shared risk.

chapters.title: The Loaf That Tastes Like 1979
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the public graduation-week bake sale, Ulyana bakes the complete recipe in front of the town using the east wing's original oven, smuggled open one last time. Everyone who eats remembers Elias — his voice, his fall, the cover-up — simultaneously. Beat: climax begins; collective memory as public testimony.

chapters.title: Margaret Harrow, Cornered
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Confrontation at the emergency board session: Margaret admits her father's crime but argues exposing it destroys the scholarships, the fund, Theo's sister's care — the price of truth made explicit. Ulyana answers: Elias deserved to be remembered more than the Harrows deserved peace. Beat: moral climax; no clean victory offered.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The board votes to preserve the east wing as a memorial, rename the scholarship for Elias Okafor, and refer the fund's history to state investigators — meaning the Vasquez payments end. Theo testifies anyway, choosing truth with his eyes open. Beat: costly resolution; Theo's arc completes.

chapters.title: Graduation
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Eleven days served in full: Ulyana walks at graduation, gives the student address beside Elias's name on the new plaque, and watches Margaret Harrow resign in silence. The bread she bakes now tastes plain and honest — her grief-baked gift is gone, traded for the town's memory. Beat: bittersweet triumph; the price paid, named.

chapters.title: A New Starter
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. Summer: Ulyana reopens the bakery part-time, cultivating a new starter from Ida's last loaf, and writes her own first recipe card — instructions for whoever needs the walls to talk next. Theo bags flour beside her. Beat: quiet hope; belonging chosen rather than inherited, and a legacy begun.
